content.title: About
content.content: Toasted pumpernickel bread is a whole‑grain rye loaf made from whole rye flour, a natural starter, and a pinch of salt. After baking, the slices are toasted until a golden‑brown crust forms, giving a crunchy texture and deepening the nutty, caramel‑like flavor.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Pumpernickel is traditionally considered more nutritious than white bread because of its higher fiber content.
Toasting enhances aroma and creates a satisfying crunch, making it popular for open‑face sandwiches and snacks.
Rye bread is a staple in Scandinavian and Eastern European cuisines, often served with soups, fish, or cured meats.
The dark color comes from using whole rye grain and sometimes adding molasses or honey during baking.

items.title: High in fiber
items.content: Pumpernickel provides both soluble and insoluble fiber, supporting digestive health and promoting satiety.

items.title: Low glycemic index
items.content: Compared with white bread, rye releases glucose more slowly, helping to stabilize blood sugar levels.

items.title: B‑vitamin source
items.content: The bread contains thiamine, niacin, and folate, which are essential for energy metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: It supplies iron, magnesium, and zinc, important for blood formation and immune support.

items.title: Antioxidants
items.content: Dark rye grains contain phenolic compounds that act as antioxidants.

items.title: Gluten
items.content: Pumpernickel contains gluten and is not suitable for people with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Some varieties can be salty; individuals monitoring sodium intake should check the label.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Toasted slices have slightly higher calories due to added oil during toasting.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Toasted pumpernickel works well for open‑face sandwiches, as a base for avocado toast, croutons in soups, or paired with cheese and cured meats. Lightly brush with olive oil and sprinkle seeds for extra flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the bread in a paper bag or bread box at room temperature for up to 3‑4 days. For longer storage, freeze slices in an airtight bag and thaw as needed.

bread-white-special-formula-added-fiber.title: White Bread, Special Formula, Added Fiber

content.title: About
content.content: White bread made with a special formula and added dietary fiber is a loaf produced from high‑grade wheat flour enriched with extra fiber to boost its nutritional value. The bread has a soft crumb, light crust, and a mild neutral flavor, suitable for eating plain or as a base for sandwiches.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Fiber in the bread improves digestion and promotes a feeling of fullness.
The special formula keeps the loaf tender even with the higher fiber content.
White bread is traditionally a source of quick‑release carbs, but added fiber slows absorption.
The product is made without preservatives, making it more natural.
Bread is often used as a base for open‑face sandwiches and appetizers.

items.title: Supports Digestive Health
items.content: Dietary fiber helps maintain regular bowel movements and supports a healthy gut microbiome.

items.title: Lower Glycemic Impact
items.content: Added fiber slows glucose absorption, helping to moderate blood sugar spikes.

items.title: Increases Satiety
items.content: Fiber prolongs the feeling of fullness, which can aid in weight management.

items.title: Source of B‑Vitamins
items.content: Wheat flour provides thiamine, riboflavin, and niacin, essential for energy metabolism.

items.title: Mineral Content
items.content: The loaf contains iron, magnesium, and phosphorus, supporting blood and bone health.

items.title: Gluten Allergy
items.content: Bread made from wheat contains gluten, which can trigger reactions in people with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

items.title: Glycemic Index Considerations
items.content: Despite the added fiber, the base is still white flour, so individuals with diabetes should monitor portion sizes.

items.title: Sodium Content
items.content: The product may contain moderate salt; those limiting sodium should account for it in their overall diet.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: The bread works well toasted, as a sandwich base, alongside soups and salads, or crumbled into casseroles. It can also be used for open‑face toppings with vegetables and lean proteins.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the loaf in a cool, dry place in a paper bag or bread box. For longer storage, freeze it and thaw at room temperature before use.

chicken-with-noodles-and-cheese-sauce-di.title: Chicken with noodles and cheese sauce, diet frozen meal

content.title: About
content.content: Chicken with noodles and cheese sauce is a diet frozen meal designed for quick and convenient preparation. It contains lean chicken breast, whole‑grain noodles, and a creamy low‑fat cheese sauce. The product is aimed at people who watch their calorie intake but do not want to sacrifice flavor.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The meal can be ready in 3–5 minutes using a microwave or stovetop.
The cheese sauce is low in saturated fat while retaining a smooth texture.
Chicken breast undergoes double thermal processing to ensure safety.
Noodles are made from whole‑grain flour, increasing fiber content.
One serving provides approximately 250 kcal, fitting many diet plans.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: Chicken breast supplies complete protein essential for maintaining muscle mass.

items.title: Low fat content
items.content: Reduced fat in the sauce helps control calorie intake and supports healthy cholesterol levels.

items.title: Fiber from whole‑grain noodles
items.content: Whole‑grain noodles aid digestion and promote satiety.

items.title: Calcium from cheese sauce
items.content: Despite being low‑fat, the sauce retains calcium important for bone health.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Chicken and whole‑grain noodles provide vitamins B6 and B12, supporting energy metabolism.

items.title: Dairy allergy
items.content: The cheese sauce may trigger reactions in individuals with lactose intolerance or milk allergy.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Monitor overall daily salt intake to avoid elevated blood pressure.

items.title: Complete heating required
items.content: Insufficiently heated meals may contain live bacteria; heat to an internal temperature of at least 75 °C.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Heat the frozen meal in a microwave or on the stovetop, stirring thoroughly to distribute the sauce evenly. Serve hot; optionally add fresh vegetables or herbs to increase volume and nutrients.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the product frozen at –18 °C or lower. Once thawed, consume within 24 hours and do not refreeze. Discard if any off‑odor or discoloration appears.

content.title: About
content.content: Frozen mocha coffee drink, decaffeinated is a refreshing beverage made from milk, cocoa powder and decaffeinated espresso, served as a thick frappe. It combines the creamy taste of milk, aromatic chocolate and a subtle coffee bitterness, but contains no caffeine, making it suitable for children and caffeine‑sensitive individuals.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Mocha coffee originated in Italy in the early 1920s as a blend of espresso and hot chocolate.
Decaffeination is usually performed by water‑process or CO₂ extraction, preserving most flavor compounds.
Frozen coffee drinks are especially popular in summer and are often served in tall glasses with a straw.
Sugar content in the finished product typically ranges from 8 % to 12 % depending on the recipe.
The cocoa used in mocha is rich in flavonoids, which have antioxidant properties.

items.title: Low caffeine content
items.content: The absence of caffeine makes the drink safe for people sensitive to stimulants and allows consumption at any time of day.

items.title: Calcium source
items.content: The milk base provides a substantial amount of calcium, essential for bone and teeth health.

items.title: Antioxidants from cocoa
items.content: Cocoa flavonoids help combat free radicals and support cardiovascular health.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Decaffeinated coffee retains vitamins B2 and B3, which are involved in energy metabolism.

items.title: Hydration
items.content: The high water content in the frozen form contributes to overall hydration.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: High sugar levels can contribute to weight gain and increase the risk of dental caries, so moderate consumption is advised.

items.title: Lactose intolerance
items.content: The drink contains milk; lactose‑intolerant individuals should choose a lactose‑free version.

items.title: Cocoa allergy
items.content: Rarely, an allergic reaction to cocoa powder may occur.

items.title: Artificial additives
items.content: Some formulations may contain flavorings and stabilizers; people avoiding additives should check the ingredient list.

content.title: How to Enjoy
content.content: Serve the frozen mocha coffee drink in a tall glass with a straw, optionally top with whipped cream, sprinkle grated chocolate or cinnamon. Garnish with berries or mint for extra flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the product in a freezer at –18 °C or lower. After thawing, consume within 24 hours. Prevent moisture from entering the packaging to avoid ice crystal formation.

content.title: About
content.content: Canned grapefruit consists of sliced wedges or halves of grapefruit packed in glass or metal jars with syrup or its own juice. The canning process preserves most of the fruit's flavor and nutrients while providing a long shelf life without refrigeration.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Grapefruit was first cultivated in the early 19th century in the Caribbean as a hybrid of pomelo and sweet orange.
Canning retains a high amount of vitamin C, although it is slightly lower than in fresh fruit.
The syrup used in jars often contains a modest amount of sugar to balance the natural bitterness of grapefruit.
Canned grapefruit is frequently used in salads, desserts, and seafood dishes.

items.title: Rich in vitamin C
items.content: Vitamin C supports the immune system, aids collagen synthesis, and acts as an antioxidant.

items.title: Contains potassium
items.content: Potassium helps regulate fluid balance and supports normal heart function.

items.title: Low‑calorie food
items.content: Canned grapefruit is low in calories, making it a suitable choice for weight‑management diets.

items.title: Source of dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber promotes healthy digestion and contributes to a feeling of fullness.

items.title: Flavonoids
items.content: Flavonoids such as naringenin have anti‑inflammatory and antioxidant properties.

items.title: Bitterness
items.content: Some people may find canned grapefruit overly bitter, especially if the fruit was not fully ripe before processing.

items.title: Drug interactions
items.content: Grapefruit can affect the metabolism of certain medications, potentially increasing their effects.

items.title: Added sugar in syrup
items.content: The syrup may add extra sugar, which should be considered by individuals with diabetes.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Canned grapefruit can be eaten straight from the jar, added to fruit salads, yogurts, smoothies, used in desserts, or served as a side with seafood. Drain excess syrup before serving if desired.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store unopened jars in a cool, dry place. Once opened, keep the jar refrigerated in its original container and consume within 5–7 days.

content.title: About
content.content: McDouble is a double burger from McDonald’s, made of two beef patties, a slice of cheese, onions, pickles, mustard and ketchup, all sandwiched between two buns.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The McDouble was introduced in 1997 as a lower‑price alternative to the Double Cheeseburger.
It contains about 390 calories, making it less caloric than the classic Double Cheeseburger.
In some countries the burger can be served without onions upon request.
The McDouble is often featured in “2 for $X” promotions.
It is popular among students because of its price and size.

items.title: Protein source
items.content: Two beef patties provide roughly 20 g of protein, essential for muscle repair.

items.title: Contains iron
items.content: Beef supplies heme iron, which is more readily absorbed by the body.

items.title: Calcium content
items.content: The cheese adds calcium, important for bones and teeth.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Beef and the bun provide B12 and niacin, supporting energy metabolism.

items.title: Energy boost
items.content: Carbohydrates in the bun give a quick source of energy.

items.title: High sodium
items.content: Ketchup and pickles make the burger high in sodium, which can be an issue for hypertension.

items.title: Saturated fats
items.content: Beef patties and cheese contain saturated fats, which should be limited in heart‑healthy diets.

items.title: Dairy allergy
items.content: Cheese may trigger reactions in people with lactose intolerance or milk allergy.

items.title: Gluten
items.content: The bun contains wheat, so the product is not suitable for a gluten‑free diet.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: McDouble is typically served in its standard packaging and can be eaten as a standalone snack or paired with fries and a drink. You can customize it with extra sauces or omit ingredients such as onions.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store a prepared McDouble in the refrigerator for no more than 24 hours. For longer storage, reheat in a microwave or oven to retain flavor and texture.

content.title: About
content.content: Non-alcoholic wine is a beverage made from grapes with the alcohol removed or reduced to a very low level (usually below 0.5%). It retains the aromatic and flavor characteristics of traditional wine but without the intoxicating effect. Production methods include vacuum distillation, reverse osmosis, or fermentation followed by alcohol extraction.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The first non-alcoholic wine, called "Mochiboo," appeared in Japan in the 1970s.
In the United States, non-alcoholic wine is often used in cooking as a substitute for regular wine in sauces and marinades.
Flavor profiles range from dry to sweet, similar to conventional wines.
Some brands add natural berry extracts and spices to enhance aroma.
Non-alcoholic wine is popular among pregnant women and those who abstain from alcohol for religious or health reasons.

items.title: Rich in antioxidants
items.content: Like regular wine, non-alcoholic wine contains polyphenols such as resveratrol, which help protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Supports cardiovascular health
items.content: Polysaccharides and flavonoids may improve vascular function without the risks associated with alcohol.

items.title: Low in calories
items.content: Non-alcoholic wine typically has fewer calories than its alcoholic counterpart, making it more diet‑friendly.

items.title: Contains B‑vitamins
items.content: Fermentation produces small amounts of B1, B2, and B6 vitamins, beneficial for metabolism.

items.title: Hydration
items.content: Unlike alcoholic drinks, non-alcoholic wine does not cause dehydration and can contribute to fluid balance.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Some sweet varieties may raise blood sugar levels.

items.title: Sulfite content
items.content: Like regular wine, it often contains sulfites, which can trigger allergic reactions in sensitive individuals.

items.title: Added additives
items.content: Flavor enhancers and preservatives may be used; check the label if you have dietary restrictions.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve chilled as an aperitif, use in cocktails, or substitute for regular wine in cooking—sauces, risotto, and marinades.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the bottle in a cool, dark place with the cap tightly closed. After opening, keep it refrigerated and consume within 3–5 days.
